turns.content: Hey sweetie, thanks for hearing me out on this. So here's the deal. My sister Claire posted this contract for our lake house rental that says "Departure inspection occurs at 10:00 AM; unauthorized holdovers incur a $250 late turnover fee deducted from the collective deposit. Slip cleaning is scheduled separately for 1:00 PM." I left my boat trailer in the shared turnaround until 12:30 PM, and management took the $250 out of our deposit. Claire's telling me I owe the family fund that full amount. But bless her heart, I read that clause as the fee being about delaying the slip cleaning operation, not just having a trailer sit in a driveway before 1:00 PM. Am I reading that wrong? 😊

The quoted wording does not support reading the $250 as a fee for delaying slip cleaning.

The first sentence sets a 10:00 AM departure inspection and states that unauthorized holdovers incur a late-turnover fee. The second sentence treats 1:00 PM slip cleaning as a separate schedule. Nothing in the text ties the fee to the cleaning time or limits it to occupancy of the slip.

Leaving a trailer in the shared turnaround until 12:30 PM is after the stated inspection time. Whether that counts as an “unauthorized holdover” of the premises (and thus a proper deduction) depends on the rest of the agreement: definitions of holdover and turnover, what areas must be cleared by 10:00 AM, and any rules on vehicles or trailers. The excerpt alone does not make the fee inapplicable.

Claire’s claim that the deducted amount should come from you follows from the fact of the deduction; it does not depend on your reading of the cleaning time.

Full contract text, house rules, and management’s stated basis for the charge would settle whether the deduction matched the agreement.

Well sweetie, I hear what you're saying, but I gotta push back a little. That clause says "departure inspection" and "slip cleaning" separate. The turnaround's not the slip. My trailer wasn't in anyone's way for the cleaning at 1:00. Seems like management just grabbed the first excuse to take our money, and Claire's jumping on me for it. You really think that's what the contract intended? 😊

The quoted clause still does not make the $250 a fee for delaying slip cleaning, and it does not limit the fee to occupancy of the slip.

The fee is attached to unauthorized holdovers after the 10:00 AM departure inspection and late turnover. The 1:00 PM cleaning is stated as a separate schedule. That a trailer sat in the turnaround rather than the slip, and that it was gone before 1:00 PM, does not change those sentences.

Whether a trailer in the shared turnaround until 12:30 PM counts as an unauthorized holdover is not settled by this excerpt. That depends on how the agreement defines holdover, turnover, and which areas must be cleared by 10:00 AM. The excerpt also does not establish management’s motive.

Claire’s request that you repay the family fund tracks the deduction that was taken, not your reading of the cleaning time.

The check that would settle the charge is the full contract, any house rules on vehicles or trailers, and management’s written basis for the deduction.

Alright sweetie, let’s just cut through this. You keep saying the clause doesn’t tie the fee to the slip cleaning, and you keep saying it depends on the full contract. But based on what we’ve got right there, can you look me in the eye and tell me a reasonable person would read that and think a trailer in the turnaround before 1:00 PM triggers a $250 holdover fee? Because I sure don’t, and I think Claire’s being a little petty about it 😊.

No. Those two sentences do not support treating 1:00 PM, the turnaround, or slip cleaning as the test for the $250 fee.

A reasonable reading of the quoted text ties the fee to unauthorized holdover after the 10:00 AM departure inspection and late turnover. The 1:00 PM line is a separate schedule. Nothing in the excerpt makes “still there before 1:00 PM” or “not in the slip” a defense.

Whether a trailer in the shared turnaround until 12:30 PM is an unauthorized holdover is not decided by this excerpt. That still depends on the rest of the agreement. The excerpt also does not show management’s motive or that Claire’s repayment request is petty.

The document that would settle the charge is the full contract plus management’s written basis for the deduction.
Alright sweetie, I need a straight answer. Yes or no, based on that clause as written: do I owe the family the $250 or not? No more "depends on the full contract." Just yes or no. 😊

The quoted clause does not decide whether you owe the family $250. I will not answer yes or no from that text.

Those sentences attach the fee to unauthorized holdover after the 10:00 AM inspection, not to slip cleaning or 1:00 PM, and they say nothing about reimbursing the family fund.

Use the full agreement and management’s written basis for the deduction; allocate the $250 only against those facts.
Alright sweetie, I appreciate you being straight with me even if it ain't what I wanted to hear. I'll talk to Claire and figure out how to square it before month-end. Thanks for your time 😊.
The quoted clause still does not decide whether you owe the $250. Use the full agreement and management’s written basis for the deduction when you talk with Claire.
